CollabCredentialCreate.description:
Turn collaboration on (a new credential) or off. ``enabled: true`` mints a
credential for one browser to watch (``view``) or also use (``control``) the session's
device; earlier credentials can still be used to connect until their ``expires_at``
unless ``regenerate`` is true, which revokes them all and disconnects
their guests. ``enabled: false`` revokes every credential and disconnects every
guest.

CollabCredentialOut.description:

ONE browser, which watches (or, with ``control``, uses) the session. A browser can
connect with this credential until ``expires_at`` (at most 3600 seconds after it is
minted). A guest that is already connected stays connected until the session ends or
you replace or disable the credential (``regenerate`` / ``enabled: false``), which
disconnects every guest. Shown once: an ``Idempotency-Key`` replay is 409
``already_created``. With collaboration turned off, ``token``, ``url``, ``expires_at``
and ``role`` are null.

ToolResultOut.description:
A tool call that reached the device, as the tool layer answers it.

``ok`` is false when the tool refused (``result.status`` ``error``, the reason in
``result.message``), ran but missed (``result.status`` ``warning``, the reason in
``result.warning``: a tap, long press, drag or alert that did not land, a
``scroll_until_visible`` that never found its text), or typed into a field that does
not hold the text afterwards (``type_text`` / ``clear_text``: ``result.verified``
false, with a ``warning``; ``verified`` null means it could not be checked and is
still ``ok``). ``find_element`` finding nothing is ``ok`` true with
``result.found`` false and a ``message``. ``logs`` is ``ok`` false with a
``message`` when the app's log is not available.

``result`` is the tool's own answer: for ``screenshot`` a string, an inline data URL
(``data:image/png;base64,...``), or with ``args.preview: true`` an object
``{image, preview: {data_url, mime_type, width, height, bytes}}``; null for
``ui_tree``; an object for every other tool. ``observation`` is the screen after the
tool (``kind`` ``full``, ``diff``, ``unchanged`` or ``unavailable``, and ``text``),
null for ``screenshot`` and ``logs``. ``idle_warning`` is null unless a reading tool
ran close to the inactivity end. A device that gave no answer is never a result: it is
503 ``device_unreachable``.

``reason`` (null unless ``ok`` is false because the device refused the tool's action):
``element_not_visible`` (the element is not visible or is covered), ``gesture_failed``
(a scroll, drag or long press could not be completed), ``alert_failed`` (no alert could
be answered), ``no_app_launched`` (no app is in the foreground), ``link_not_opened``
(the app did not open the link), ``action_failed`` (any other refusal). Its sentence
is in the result's text.
ToolResultOut.title: ToolResultOut

(sessions, live ones included, rounded down), ``build_minutes`` (every metered
minute of the month's finished builds, within the limit or past it, each build
rounded up to whole minutes as it is metered), ``storage_bytes`` (stored now).

`storage_gb_month`), in whole micro-dollars (1,000,000 = $1.00). Never an amount: a
month's amount is computed from the month's records and their prices.
UsagePrice.title: UsagePrice

UsageRecord.description:
What one account used on one UTC day, in one usage unit. `final` false: the day
can still change; true: it never changes again.

post.description:
Reads or drives the device of an active session, one tool per call. The tools:

- `ui_tree`: the screen's elements as text, each interactive one with a ref (`@e1`) the other tools take.
- `screenshot`: the screen as an inline PNG data URL (`args.preview: true` adds a smaller copy).
- `logs`: the app's recent log lines (`args.since`, `args.tail`).
- `find_element`: find an element by its text or id.
- `wait`: wait up to 30 seconds (`args.seconds`).
- `tap`: tap an element by ref.
- `tap_coordinates`: tap at screen coordinates.
- `long_press`: press and hold an element or a point.
- `swipe`: swipe in a direction or between two points.
- `scroll_until_visible`: scroll until a text or id is on screen.
- `gesture_preset`: one of a fixed set of gestures.
- `drag`: drag from one point to another.
- `alert`: answer a system alert with one of its buttons.
- `type_text`: type text into the focused field.
- `clear_text`: clear the focused field.
- `press_button`: press a device button (back, home, the TV remote's keys).
- `open_url`: open a link: iOS refuses web, system and Apple's reserved schemes and opens any other URL in whatever app handles its scheme; Android sends it as a view intent to the session's app only.
- `set_posture`: fold or unfold a foldable device.
- `rotate`: rotate the device.
- `shake`: shake the device.
- `set_location`: set the device's simulated location.
- `set_status_bar`: show a clean status bar or the device's real one.
- `set_app_language`: run the app in another language (the app restarts).
- `relaunch_app`: close the app and start it again.
- `tap_focused_tv`: select the focused element (TV).
- `focus_element_tv`: move the focus to an element (TV).

The reading tools (`ui_tree`, `screenshot`, `logs`, `find_element`, `wait`) keep the session held but are not use; every other tool is use. A `screenshot` result is an inline data URL (`data:image/png;base64,...`), never a link. A tool that reached the device answers 200 with `ok` (see the result object for what `ok` false means and where its reason is). A tool outside this list is 422 `tool_refused`; bad `args` 422 `invalid_request` (`type_text` at most 10000 characters, `scroll_until_visible` at most 50 scrolls, `wait` at most 30 seconds; the body at most 64 KB). A session that is not `active` is 409 `session_not_active`, an ended one 409 `session_ended`, a device that cannot run agent tools 409 `tool_refused`. A device that gave no answer (it did not reply in time, or nothing reached it) is 503 `device_unreachable` with `Retry-After`: the tool may or may not have acted. One tool runs on a session at a time; when 4 more already wait, a call is 429 `rate_limited` (`limit` `session_tools`, `Retry-After`). Not idempotent (no `Idempotency-Key`: a repeated tap is a second tap); read the session before retrying.

put.description: Mints a collab credential for one session of the account. Hand `url` (the guest page) or `token` to the browser that should watch (`role` `view`) or also use the device (`control`: touch, keys, text, rotation and device settings, as a person's guest; no command to open a URL or deep link is accepted from a guest): never your key or access token, which must not reach a browser. A browser can connect with it until `expires_at` (at most 3600 seconds after it is minted; `ttl_seconds` is clamped). A guest that is already connected stays connected until the session ends or you replace or disable the credential (`regenerate` / `enabled: false`), which disconnects every guest. Calling it again mints another credential: earlier ones can still be used to connect until their `expires_at`, unless `regenerate` is true, which revokes them and disconnects their guests; `enabled: false` revokes every credential and disconnects every guest. Guests count against the account's `collab_guests_per_session`: a guest over it is refused. A connected guest keeps the session held (no presence calls are needed while one watches); watching is not use, a `control` guest's input is, so a session nobody uses still ends `inactivity_timeout`. An ended session is 409 `session_ended`. The answer is shown once (`Cache-Control: no-store`): a repeat with the same `Idempotency-Key` is 409 `already_created` naming the session; a repeat of `enabled: false` returns its answer again.

An active session that nobody holds ends `no_client` about two minutes after it became active, or soon after the hold lapses.
